subsystems.name: Logical patches
subsystems.role: each logical qubit is a rectangular tile of physical qubits running the surface code, with boundaries of two alternating types.

subsystems.name: The seam
subsystems.role: the strip of stabilisers along the touching edge of two patches, which is switched on and off during a merge and a split.

subsystems.name: Syndrome extraction
subsystems.role: measures every stabiliser each cycle to detect errors without destroying the encoded state.

subsystems.name: Classical control and decoder
subsystems.role: turns measurement bits into corrections, fast enough to keep up with the qubit cycle.

subsystems.name: Pauli frame
subsystems.role: a software record of the byproduct X, Z and Y operators created by merge and split outcomes, applied later rather than physically.

subsystems.name: Compilation layer
subsystems.role: schedules merges, splits and patch moves into a fault-tolerant circuit.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the qubit array
buildSteps.detail: Build a grid of physical qubits with nearest-neighbour coupling so that a patch can be laid out as a checkerboard of data and measure qubits.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the surface code
buildSteps.detail: Tune single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates and readout until the physical error rate sits below the surface-code threshold — currently around the 1% level per operation, with the best gates an order of magnitude better.

buildSteps.title: Initialise and verify patches
buildSteps.detail: Prepare each logical qubit in a known state and run repeated stabiliser cycles, decoding the syndromes to confirm the patch is error-corrected.

buildSteps.title: Merge two patches
buildSteps.detail: Stop measuring the stabilisers on the facing boundaries, then start measuring the new stabilisers that straddle the gap. The two tiles become one larger tile.

buildSteps.title: Measure across the merged patch
buildSteps.detail: While merged, read out joint logical operators — for example the Z of both qubits at once — which is what transfers the logical information.

buildSteps.title: Split the patches apart
buildSteps.detail: Measure the original boundary stabilisers in the complementary basis, cutting the large tile back into two separate logical qubits.

buildSteps.title: Track the byproducts
buildSteps.detail: The parity of the merge and split outcomes tells the controller which X, Z or Y correction the logical state picked up. Record it in the Pauli frame instead of applying a pulse.

buildSteps.title: Decode across the seam
buildSteps.detail: Run the decoder over the combined history of both patches, treating the seam measurements as part of one matching graph, so errors near the boundary are caught.

buildSteps.title: Compose gates
buildSteps.detail: Chain merges and splits — a logical CNOT uses a few of them, and multi-qubit Paulis are read directly — building up a full Clifford gate set, then add magic states for universality.

prerequisites.why: small experiments now show logical error rates falling as code distance grows, the effect lattice surgery depends on.

prerequisites.tech: High-fidelity two-qubit gates and single-shot readout
prerequisites.why: below-threshold operation needs gate and measurement errors well under 1%, achieved on some platforms but not yet at the scale of a processor.
syndromes must be decoded within the qubit cycle, and current demonstrations mostly decode offline.
lattice surgery exists precisely to fit planar hardware where distant qubits cannot interact directly.
merging gives Clifford gates only; non-Clifford gates need injected magic states, which are costly to prepare.
the number of physical qubits and cycles per logical gate must come down for algorithms to fit.

pathway.milestone: surface-code patches operated and corrected on small grids, with logical error rates measured against code distance
pathway.unlocks: confidence that adding qubits really does suppress errors.

pathway.milestone: a fault-tolerant logical two-qubit gate between two patches, with the seam decoded live
pathway.unlocks: the basic unit of lattice surgery proven end to end on hardware.

pathway.milestone: a compiled logical circuit combining merges, splits and magic-state injection
pathway.unlocks: a universal, error-corrected gate set on one processor.

pathway.milestone: tiled arrays of many patches with automated routing
pathway.unlocks: running small quantum algorithms whose logical error rate is far below any single physical qubit.
